pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
🎯 **By the end of this lesson you will be able to:**
- Collect and list different types of agricultural tools used for farm activities.
- Match each tool with the familiar type of agricultural activity it is used for, and create an album of the tools.

pages.title: What are Basic and Simple Agricultural Tools?
pages.body: Basic and simple agricultural tools are hand operated implements used by farmers to carry out everyday farm tasks, such as clearing land, tilling soil, planting, weeding, watering, transporting materials and harvesting. Unlike large, engine powered farm machinery, these tools generally rely on the physical effort of the person using them, often combined with the mechanical advantage of a simple machine, such as a lever or a wedge, built into the tool's design.

questions.q: Basic and simple agricultural tools are best described as
o: Hand operated implements used for everyday farm tasks
Tools with no practical use on a farm
questions.e: Basic and simple agricultural tools are hand operated implements used by farmers to carry out everyday farm tasks, such as clearing land, tilling soil, planting, weeding, watering, transporting materials and harvesting.

pages.title: Common Basic and Simple Agricultural Tools
pages.body:
Cutlasses, hoes, rakes, watering cans, wheelbarrows and sickles are six commonly used basic and simple agricultural tools, each suited to a particular type of farm activity, as summarised in the table below.

| **TOOL** | **MAIN USE** | **TYPICAL FARM ACTIVITY** |
|---|---|---|
| **Cutlass** | Cutting and clearing bush, weeds and small branches | Clearing land before planting |
| **Hoe** | Tilling, turning and loosening soil | Preparing seed beds and weeding |
| **Rake** | Gathering leaves, grass and other debris | Clearing and tidying a garden or seed bed |
| **Watering can** | Applying water evenly to plants and seedlings | Watering a nursery bed or young crops |
| **Wheelbarrow** | Carrying soil, produce, tools or manure | Transporting materials around the farm |
| **Sickle** | Cutting and harvesting crops close to the ground | Harvesting rice, grasses or similar crops |

pages.title: Matching Tools to Farm Activities
pages.body: Land clearing, soil preparation, planting, weeding, watering, transporting and harvesting are seven broad categories of farm activities, and matching the correct tool to each activity is an important practical skill for effective and efficient farming. Using the wrong tool for a task, such as trying to clear thick bush with only a rake, can waste time and energy, while using the right tool, such as a cutlass, can make the same task quick and manageable.

questions.q: Which tool is mainly used for cutting and clearing bush and weeds?
questions.e: Using the wrong tool for a task, such as trying to clear thick bush with only a rake, can waste time and energy, while using the right tool, such as a cutlass, can make the same task quick and manageable.

questions.e: When using a watering can, the user should tilt it gently and move it steadily over the plants to ensure even watering without damaging delicate seedlings.

questions.e: The cutlass has a long, sharp blade suited to cutting through bush and small branches, the hoe has a flat, angled blade suited to turning soil, and the wheelbarrow has a single wheel and a wide carrying tray suited to transporting loose materials such as soil…

questions.e: When using a sickle to harvest crops, the user should grip the crop stems firmly with one hand and cut with a smooth, controlled motion, keeping fingers well away from the blade.

pages.title: Going further
pages.body:
> 💡 **Going further**

Proper maintenance of agricultural tools, such as cleaning them after use, sharpening blades regularly, and storing them in a dry place, helps extend their working life and keeps them safe and effective to use. A well maintained cutlass, for example, cuts more efficiently and requires less physical effort than a blunt, rusty one, which also reduces the risk of accidents caused by tools slipping during use.

Using tools until they break completely

pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
🎯 **By the end of this lesson you will be able to:**
- Explain how the different agricultural tools are used on a farm or school garden to perform specific agricultural activities.
- Practise the use of different agricultural tools for specific activities on a farm or school garden.
- Select appropriate tools for specific agriculture tasks.

pages.title: From Knowing Tools to Using Them Correctly
pages.body: Building on Lesson 12, where the main basic and simple agricultural tools were identified and matched to general activities, this lesson focuses on actually engaging in the correct, practical use of these tools on a farm or in a school garden. Knowing what a tool is called and what it is generally used for is an important first step, but developing the correct technique for holding, positioning and operating each tool safely is equally important for effective farm work.

lessons.subject: sci
lessons.title: How Agricultural Tools are Used to Perform Specific Activities

pages.title: How Agricultural Tools are Used to Perform Specific Activities
pages.body:
Correct grip, posture, technique and safety awareness are four important considerations when using any agricultural tool for a specific farm activity.

- When using a cutlass to clear bush, the user should hold it firmly with a full grip, swing it with a controlled motion away from the body, and keep other people at a safe distance.

- When using a hoe to till soil, the user should hold the handle firmly with both hands, bend at the knees rather than the back, and use short, controlled strokes to turn the soil evenly.

- When using a watering can, the user should tilt it gently and move it steadily over the plants to ensure even watering without damaging delicate seedlings.

- When using a wheelbarrow, the user should load it evenly, keep their back straight, and lift using their legs rather than their back when starting to move it.

- When using a sickle to harvest crops, the user should grip the crop stems firmly with one hand and cut with a smooth, controlled motion, keeping fingers well away from the blade.

pages.title: Selecting Appropriate Tools for Specific Tasks
pages.body:
Matching each farm activity to its most suitable tool, and understanding the reason behind that choice, is an important practical skill developed through repeated engagement with real farm or garden tasks, as shown in the table below.

| **FARM ACTIVITY** | **MOST APPROPRIATE TOOL** | **REASON FOR CHOICE** |
|---|---|---|
| **Clearing thick bush before planting** | Cutlass | Its long, sharp blade cuts through woody stems and weeds effectively |
| **Preparing a seed bed** | Hoe | Its flat, angled blade is well suited to turning and loosening soil |
| **Watering a nursery bed** | Watering can | Its perforated spout spreads water gently and evenly over seedlings |
| **Transporting harvested produce** | Wheelbarrow | Its wheel and tray allow heavy loads to be moved with less effort |
| **Harvesting rice or similar crops** | Sickle | Its curved blade cuts crop stems close to the ground efficiently |

questions.q: When using a cutlass to clear bush, it is important to
o: Hold it loosely with one finger
Keep other people at a safe distance while swinging it
Swing it directly towards other people
Use it without checking the surroundings
questions.e: When using a cutlass to clear bush, the user should hold it firmly with a full grip, swing it with a controlled motion away from the body, and keep other people at a safe distance.

questions.q: When using a hoe to till soil, the correct posture involves
o: Bending at the knees rather than the back
Bending only at the back and not the knees
Standing completely still with no movement
Using the hoe only above waist height
questions.e: When using a hoe to till soil, the user should hold the handle firmly with both hands, bend at the knees rather than the back, and use short, controlled strokes to turn the soil evenly.

questions.q: When using a watering can on seedlings, it should be
o: Emptied all at once directly onto one spot
Held upside down at all times
Thrown at the plants from a distance
Tilted gently and moved steadily for even watering
questions.e: When using a watering can, the user should tilt it gently and move it steadily over the plants to ensure even watering without damaging delicate seedlings.

questions.q: When lifting a loaded wheelbarrow, a person should
o: Bend only at the back and lift with the back
Keep their back straight and lift using their legs
Load it unevenly on one side only
questions.e: When using a wheelbarrow, the user should load it evenly, keep their back straight, and lift using their legs rather than their back when starting to move it.

questions.q: When using a sickle to harvest crops, safety mainly involves
o: Cutting directly towards one's own body
Gripping stems firmly and keeping fingers away from the blade
Holding the blade with bare fingers directly
Swinging it as fast as possible with no control
questions.e: When using a sickle to harvest crops, the user should grip the crop stems firmly with one hand and cut with a smooth, controlled motion, keeping fingers well away from the blade.

questions.q: Selecting the appropriate tool for a task mainly depends on
o: The cost of the tool only
The specific requirements of the activity being performed

questions.q: Which tool would be most appropriate for transporting harvested produce across a farm?
questions.e: The cutlass has a long, sharp blade suited to cutting through bush and small branches, the hoe has a flat, angled blade suited to turning soil, and the wheelbarrow has a single wheel and a wide carrying tray suited to transporting loose materials such as soil…

questions.q: Which tool would be most appropriate for preparing a seed bed by turning the soil?

Notice that each tool requires a slightly different grip, posture and motion suited to its shape and purpose. Practising the correct technique for each tool not only makes farm work more efficient but also significantly reduces the risk of injury.

pages.title: Going further
pages.body:
> 💡 **Going further**

Regular, supervised practice using agricultural tools, whether on a family farm, a community farm, or a school garden, is one of the most effective ways to build both skill and confidence. Schools that maintain a school garden give learners a safe, structured environment to practise selecting and using the correct tool for a task, reinforcing the knowledge gained in the classroom with genuine, hands on experience.

questions.q: Practising correct tool technique mainly helps to
o: Increase the risk of injury only
Make tasks slower and less efficient
Reduce injury risk and improve efficiency
Remove the need for any tool at all

questions.q: A school garden is useful for learning agricultural tool use mainly because it
o: Has no relevance to real farm activities
Provides a safe, structured environment for practice
Replaces the need for any farm tools
questions.e: Schools that maintain a school garden give learners a safe, structured environment to practise selecting and using the correct tool for a task, reinforcing the knowledge gained in the classroom with genuine, hands on experience.
